## streams (refine independently)

### A — hygienic macro system (design: post-bootstrap)

- declarative and procedural macros; procedural macros on **bytecode VM**
- parser reserves (`!`, hygiene rules) already documented in design — keep **sv0doc** and parser aligned
- **prerequisite**: stable AST, VM, parser (design lists all three)

/ai: when starting implementation, create `task/sv0-toolchain-milestone-cross-cutting-macros.Rmd` with phased deliverables.

### B — literate `.sv0.md` tangling

- chunk names, `<<references>>`, error mapping to markdown line numbers
- integration with `sv0 doc` and doctests (`task/sv0-toolchain-milestone-2-prep.Rmd`)

/ai: add grammar/spec updates under **sv0doc** before enabling in compiler by default.

### C — standard library depth

- **`core`**: complete vs design tier 1
- **`std`**: allocator, I/O, collections, **networking**
- **concurrency**: `std::thread`, channels, `Mutex`, `Arc`, atomics (design ties to milestone 3+)
- **`crypto`**: overlaps **milestone 5**; link deliverables to avoid duplication

### D — package registry and ecosystem

- design mentions a **future** registry — track feasibility, naming, and versioning here until it becomes its own milestone file

### E — quantum simulator and other research use cases

- aspirational in design goals; no numbered milestone — use this section or a dedicated task if work begins

### F — multi-module linker and `pub` visibility (scheduled: post-M5)

- **Problem.** `--project` builds **source-concatenate** every `.sv0` under the
  directory into one translation unit ("collision-free source-concat, no arena
  merge" — an M3 expedient, `link.sv0`). No module boundaries survive: a
  non-`pub` item in one file is reachable from another, `use` clauses are
  stripped/aliased, and `pub` is a parse-accepted no-op. SPEC UP-025 (via
  sv0-strings) and the language spec both require real `pub`/private
  enforcement.
- **Scope.** Finish the M3 multi-module story: `mapProgramUnit` /
  `link.linkProjectDir` arena merge (the deferred `mapItem` rewrite), per-item
  file-origin tracking through resolve + check, and a visibility rule that
  rejects a cross-file reference to a non-`pub` item. `pub` enforcement falls
  out of the origin tracking; this also removes the flat-concat leak class the
  ad-hoc patches work around — the dup-`main` hazard (`link.sv0`
  `link_listing_root_entry_count`, SS-U09), the assembler's auto-namespacing of
  colliding type names, silent cross-file shadowing.
- **Why post-M5.** Not F0-blocking for sv0-strings (flat `module strings_*;`,
  all-`pub` surface — `pub` enforcement is a no-op there today; recorded as an
  F0 deviation). Large (parser + link + resolver + checker + lowering; high
  self-host-loop regression surface). It should not jump the M5 queue absent a
  concrete pull — e.g. sv0-strings R0.2 wanting hidden internals, or an M5
  crypto module wanting real encapsulation.
- **Do NOT** bolt a narrow visibility pass onto flat-concat first: threading
  file-origin through the resolver is most of this work anyway, so the bolt-on
  is near-full cost and thrown away by the real merge.
- Split into its own task file when work starts.
